html:
Abraham Lincoln was the 16th president of the United States, from 1861 until he was murdered in 1865. He led the Union through the American Civil War and played a central part in ending slavery.

Born in a one-room log cabin in Kentucky, he grew up on the frontier with little schooling and taught himself law. He became a lawyer, a member of the Illinois legislature and a congressman. In 1854 a new law opened western territories to slavery, and Lincoln, angered, joined the new Republican Party. His debates with Stephen Douglas in 1858 made him known across the country.

He won the presidency in 1860 on a promise to stop slavery spreading west. Seven southern states left the Union to form the Confederacy before he took office; war began in April 1861, and four more joined them. Lincoln's war aims grew as it went on:

  • At first his aim was to save the Union.
  • In 1863 his Emancipation Proclamation declared slaves in rebel areas free, and Black men were recruited into the Union army; nearly 200,000 served.
  • His Gettysburg Address of 1863 spoke of "a new birth of freedom" and government "of the people, by the people, for the people".
  • He pushed Congress to pass the 13th Amendment to the Constitution, which abolished slavery in 1865.

The Confederate army surrendered in April 1865. Five days later Lincoln was shot at a theatre in Washington by John Wilkes Booth, a Confederate sympathiser, and died the next morning. He is often ranked the greatest American president. Activists like Frederick Douglass pushed him, and later Martin Luther King Jr. spoke from the steps of his memorial.
sum: Abraham Lincoln was the 16th president of the United States, from 1861 until he was murdered in 1865. He led the Union through the American Civil War and played a central part in ending slavery.
